remarks:
North Buffalo living without the North Buffalo price tag! Welcome to 122 Heath Street, a charming 1930s two-story single-family home on a fully fenced corner lot at Heath and Bruce. Priced at $210,000, this is the kind of home first-time buyers have been waiting for: solid, freshly refreshed, and ready to move in.

A 2026 cosmetic renovation did the heavy lifting for you. New windows throughout (the only two not replaced were already vinyl), a new sliding glass door, refinished hardwood floors, fresh interior paint on the entire first floor, new carpet on the front and back stairs, exterior scraping and painting, a newly stained back deck, front walkway concrete repairs, and tree work around the property.

Step inside to original hardwood floors flowing through the foyer, living room, and dining room. The eat-in kitchen features flooring updated three years ago, and the new sliding glass door in the dining room opens right onto a private back deck, perfect for morning coffee or summer cookouts.

Upstairs you’ll find three nicely sized bedrooms, each with hardwood floors and a closet, plus a full bath with vinyl flooring and a tub surround updated about three years ago. Need more storage? There’s a walk-up attic with stair access.

The mechanicals are in good shape too. The home sits on a very strong limestone foundation and has forced air heat with a new motor installed December 2025, a hot water tank about two years old, circuit breakers, and mostly copper supply lines. The house and garage roofs are approximately 15 years old. The basement offers glass block windows with vents and laundry hookups.

Outside, enjoy a concrete driveway, a two-car detached garage, and a fully fenced yard. Pride of ownership shows here: you’ll be only the second owner since the original family who built the home.

A walkable location, a move-in ready home, and a price that makes ownership possible. Don’t miss it!

OPEN HOUSE: Tuesday, October 20, 5:00-7:00 PM. OPEN HOUSE: Sunday, 10/25/2026 from 12:00 -2:00 PM.
